Unlike standard resources that you produce via buildings or jobs, Blackcoin is strictly traded. It acts as a speculative asset that you buy and sell from the Leviathans (Elders) in exchange for Relics.

Because the price of Blackcoin fluctuates dynamically over time, the primary strategy is to treat it like a real-world stock: buy it when the price is low, and cash it out for a massive return in Relics when the price peaks.

2. Unlocking Blackcoin

To enter the cryptocurrency market, you must follow a specific late-game research path:

  • First, research Artificial Intelligence and its follow-up, Quantum Cryptography.
  • This unlocks the Blackchain technology, which costs 5,000,000 Science and 4,096 Relics.
  • Researching Blackchain officially unlocks Blackcoin and opens up its market.

3. Market Manipulation: The “Invisible Black Hand”

Once you have unlocked Blackchain, you can purchase a powerful Workshop upgrade called the Invisible Black Hand.

  • Cost: 128 Time Crystals, 64 Blackcoin, 32 Void, and 4,096 Temporal Flux.
  • The Effect: This upgrade represents the force “leading the blackcoin market”. Crucially, it grants you the option to force a market crash at the cost of Time Crystals.

By strategically forcing crashes with the Invisible Black Hand, you can bottom out the coin’s value, buy up as much Blackcoin as possible with your Relics, wait for the market to naturally recover (or smoothly rise), and then sell it back to the Leviathans to multiply your endgame Relic stockpile exponentially.

Trade and Strategic Arbitrage

Because standard production facilities like Smelters often struggle to scale efficiently enough to meet mid-game demands, iron frequently becomes a major bottleneck. To overcome this, players utilize trade arbitrage, converting high-volume resources into iron:

  • Griffins: Griffins will sell you iron in exchange for Wood. This is an incredibly powerful strategy early on, effectively allowing you to bypass the slow smelting process. Griffins yield the most iron during Autumn (+35%), but suffer penalties during Spring (-25%) and Winter (-20%).
  • Zebras: Zebras will sell you iron, plates, and titanium in exchange for Slabs. Zebras yield the most iron during Summer (+15%), but suffer penalties in Autumn (-10%) and Winter (-20%).

Primary Uses and Crafting

Iron is the critical raw material required to craft two major mid-game resources in the Workshop:

  • Metal Plates: Costs 125 Iron. Plates are heavily used for construction, particularly for Harbours.
  • Steel: Costs 100 Iron and 100 Coal. Steel is a durable metal mandatory for crafting gears, complex machinery, and advanced buildings. To optimize your steel production later in the game, the Steel Plants upgrade allows Calciners to automatically reserve 10% of their iron output and craft it into steel.

Storage Capacity

Your initial civilization can only hold 50 iron by default. Because advanced technologies and buildings require massive amounts of iron, constantly expanding your storage limits is mandatory:

  • Early/Mid Game: Iron storage is expanded by building Barns (+50), Warehouses (+25), and Harbours (+150). You can multiply these base values by purchasing workshop storage upgrades such as Expanded, Reinforced, Titanium, Alloy, and Concrete Barns and Warehouses.
  • Late Game & Space: As you progress, massive iron storage vaults become available. Accelerators (once upgraded with Energy Rifts) add +7,500 to your iron cap. In space, Moon Bases provide +9,000 iron storage, and Cryostations grant a staggering +50,000 iron storage.

item.title: Burned Paragon
item.description:
Burned Paragon provides several crucial bonuses to your civilization’s production, storage capacity, and leader traits. It operates similarly to regular Paragon and stacks with it, but with different scaling rules:

  • Production Bonus: Burned paragon provides a global production boost, but it generally has half the effectiveness of regular paragon. It stacks directly with your normal paragon bonuses. For example, having 400 regular paragon and 400 burned paragon yields a combined 285% production increase. It is highly recommended to acquire around 200 to 400 burned paragon to significantly boost your production capabilities.
  • Storage Capacity Bonus: By default, each burned paragon grants a 0.05% bonus to your storage capacity, which is half the value of regular paragon. However, this bonus undergoes a massive change when you enter the Dark Future phase. During the Dark Future, the storage bonus from burned paragon is multiplied by four, increasing to 0.2% per burned paragon. This makes it twice as effective as regular paragon for expanding storage in the deep endgame. These bonuses stack additively with your standard paragon storage bonuses.
  • Leader Trait Boost: Burned paragon also slightly increases the effectiveness of your assigned Leader’s specific trait. For instance, if you have a Merchant leader, possessing burned paragon will directly improve the formula that dictates how many Time Crystals you receive per trade with the Leviathans.

Void is the mandatory gatekeeper for Phase 3 (“Endgame”) technologies and several high-tier sciences:

  • Void Space (800k Science, 30 Time Crystals, 100 Void): This science is the prerequisite for attempting the Atheism Challenge and for unlocking the ability to build Cryochambers.

Key Benefits and Multipliers

  • Happiness: Simply holding any amount of void provides a flat +10% happiness bonus to your kittens.
  • Storage Capacity: Void Rifts (initially costing 75 void) increase your global resource storage ratio by 2%. This effect stacks additively with Event Horizons. In the extreme endgame, building approximately 50 Void Rifts is a common goal for resource scaling.
  • Energy Production: Each Void Rift increases the energy production of HR Harvesters by 10%.
  • Science Scaling: Void is required for the Void Reactors upgrade, which increases the maximum science capacity of Research Vessels and Space Beacons by 400%.

Advanced Infrastructure Costs

Void is required for constructing and maintaining endgame structures:

  • Cryochambers: Building one costs 100 void, and fixing a used cryochamber costs 500 void.
  • Dark Nova: An endgame cryptotheology building costing 7,500 void and 75k relics; it provides a 2% boost to global energy production.
  • Holy Genocide: A high-tier upgrade costing 25,000 void and 100k relics.
  • Chronosurge: Costs 750 void and enables Chronospheres to generate temporal flux yearly.
  • Temporal Press: Used to fine-tune time-crystal shattering, these cost 10 void each.

  • Hunting: Once you research Archery, you can send kittens to hunt using 100 catpower. Each hunt has a (44 + 2* hunting bonus)% chance to yield ivory. Researching workshop upgrades like Bolas, Hunting Armour, and Nanosuits increases the amount of ivory retrieved per hunt.
  • Mints: These industrial buildings provide a way to automate ivory production. When active, a Mint consumes catpower and gold to produce ivory at a rate of 0.0021% of your maximum catpower per tick.
  • Ivory Meteors: In the late game, building Ivory Citadels enables a random astronomical event called an “Ivory Meteor”. These events have a 0.05% chance of occurring per game-day for each citadel and provide a bulk amount of ivory. This is considered an excellent “AFK” source of the resource.

Strategic Uses

Ivory is essential for both trade and advanced religious development:

  • The Unicorn Era: Ivory is a core requirement for almost all advanced unicorn-related buildings in the Religion tab. This includes Ivory Towers (25k), Sky Palaces (125k), and Sunspires (750k), which are necessary to summon alicorns and generate Time Crystals.
  • Trading with Nagas: The Nagas are a neutral trade partner that buys ivory in exchange for minerals, slabs, and concrete. This trade is a critical mechanism for bypassing mineral bottlenecks, especially in Iron Will mode.
  • Happiness Buffs: Since ivory is a rare resource, its presence directly influences kitten morale. This effect can be enhanced by the Epicurianism policy, which increases the happiness bonus to 11%.

Management and Policy/

Because ivory degrades over time and is consumed by your kittens, managing its supply is important to maintain production bonuses.

  • Stoicism: This policy halves the consumption rate of ivory, helping your hoard last longer.
  • Frugality: This policy increases the resource output of your Mints by 10%.
  • Religious Boosts: Buildings like Sky Palace , , Unicorn Utopia , and Sunspire provide percentage-based increases to the amount of ivory you gain from Ivory Meteors.

item.title: Unobtainium
item.description:

Production and Acquisition

Unobtainium is generated using Lunar Outposts on Redmoon, which convert 1.75 uranium into 0.035 unobtainium per second. Production can be significantly enhanced through several methods:

  • Global Multipliers: Productivity is boosted by Space Elevators (+1%), Orbital Arrays (+2%), and the Cosmological Libertarianism policy (+15%).
  • Space Manufacturing: This workshop upgrade allows Factories to improve the effectiveness of Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays, further scaling output.
  • Celestial Cycles: During the Redmoon cycle, unobtainium output increases by 20%. If Numeromancy is researched, holding a festival during this cycle provides a 2x multiplier to unobtainium income. Conversely, the Charon cycle imposes a 10% production penalty.

Storage and Capacity

Managing unobtainium storage is a major bottleneck in late-game progression. The base capacity is 150 units, which must be expanded to reach milestones like the “Eludium Era”.

Strategic Uses

Unobtainium is a prerequisite for the most advanced technologies and upgrades in the game:

  • Metaphysics: Unlocking the Metaphysics technology requires 5 units of unobtainium.
  • Eludium: This advanced alloy is crafted using 1000 unobtainium and 2500 alloy.
  • Trading with Leviathans: Once a Black Pyramid is built, you can trade 5000 units of unobtainium to the Leviathans for Time Crystals and Relics.
  • Infrastructure Upgrades: It is required for Unobtainium Huts (which reduce hut price ratios), Unobtainium Reflectors (increasing science caps), and the construction of Markers.
  • Chronospheres: Building a Chronosphere costs 2500 units. These are vital for resets, as each Chronosphere preserves 1.5% of your unobtainium for the next run.

The “Positive Reset” Goal

For endgame players, the ultimate objective is to establish a self-sustaining reset loop. This is achieved by reaching an unobtainium capacity of at least 8.14 billion units, allowing for the construction of 100 Chronospheres. At this level, the resources carried over during a reset exceed the costs of the Chronospheres built, enabling exponential growth in subsequent runs.

item.title: Oil Storage
item.description:
The storage limit for Oil starts at a base capacity and can be increased through the construction of specific buildings and the crafting of specialized items.

Here is a breakdown of how to increase your Oil storage capacity:

Base Oil Storage

The initial, default storage capacity for Oil is 1,500.

Increasing Oil Storage Capacity

You can increase the maximum limit of Oil through the following methods:

  1. Oil Wells: The building used to produce oil, the Oil Well, also increases your maximum oil storage. Each Oil Well provides +1500 Max Oil.

  2. Tankers (Crafted Ships): Oil storage can be significantly increased by crafting and building Tankers.

    • A Tanker is a crafted item that increases the maximum oil capacity by 500 [3, 4].
    • Tankers are crafted in the Workshop, requiring 200 Ships, 1,250 Alloy, and 5 Blueprints [4].
    • The ability to craft Tankers is unlocked by researching Robotics science [4, 5].

  3. Space Structures: Late-game structures contribute to storage, particularly when combined with specific Metaphysics upgrades:

    • Cryostation: This structure’s storage capacity is affected by the T-minus cycle, which can provide a +20% boost to its storage [6, 7].
    • Cryostations are a highly useful method for increasing resource capacity, providing +750 Titanium storage per unit, among other resources [7].

The Manuscript is a critical mid-game crafted resource that serves as a bottleneck for advancing the main scientific and religious technology trees in Kittens Game.

Here is a detailed overview of Manuscripts, their production, cost, and vital strategic role:

1. Acquisition and Crafting

Manuscripts are produced in the Workshop by converting the precursor resource, Parchment, using the resource Culture.

Input Resource Base Cost per Manuscript Cost with Tradition Policy
Parchment (Crafted from Furs) 25 units 20 units
Culture (Generated by Amphitheatres/Temples) 400 units 300 units

Manuscripts are required to continue the technology line after Philosophy.

Production Sources and Boosts

  • Parchment Generation: Parchment must be crafted from Furs. Furs are acquired through Hunting using Catpower. Players are advised to Begin Crafting Parchment as Often as You Can well before they are required, as a significant amount will be needed.
  • Culture Generation: Culture is generated by Amphitheatres and Temples. Culture accumulation is slow initially.
  • Automation (Steamworks): The Steamworks building (unlocked by Machinery) can automatically print manuscripts. The Printing Press upgrade allows Steamworks to produce 0.0025 manuscripts/sec. This can be multiplied by subsequent upgrades like Offset Press and Photolithography.
  • Trade: Manuscripts can sometimes be obtained by trading with Sharks. Sharks offer 3 Manuscripts with a 15% chance if you have an Embassy Level of 10.
  • Policy Bonus: The Tradition policy reduces the manuscript cost by 100 culture and 5 parchment, and it doubles the manuscript maximum culture effect. Choosing Tradition is generally recommended to accelerate the manuscript grind.

2. Strategic Importance and Uses

Manuscripts represent the primary bottleneck in the early-to-mid game, transitioning resource focus from Wood/Minerals toward cultural and faith production.

  • Technology Advancement: Manuscripts are necessary inputs for critical mid-game sciences:
    • Theology: Requires 35 Manuscripts.
    • Astronomy: Requires 65 Manuscripts.
    • Navigation: Requires 100 Manuscripts.
  • Next Tier Crafting: Manuscripts are refined in the Workshop, along with Science, to produce Compendiums. Compendiums are prerequisites for technologies like Architecture, Physics, and Geology.
  • Blueprint Production: Eventually, Compendiums are crafted into Blueprints, making manuscripts foundational to the late-game crafting resource chain.
  • Temple Building: Manuscripts are required to construct Temples. A single Temple costs 10 Manuscripts.
  • Culture Capacity: Manuscripts grant a minor bonus to the maximum capacity of Culture, though this effect is subject to diminishing returns.
  • Lizard Relations: The Lizard Relations: [Priests] ( /job/priest/) policy allows manuscripts to grant maximum Faith equal to the maximum culture they grant, while reducing the maximum culture they provide by 25%.

3. Overcoming the Manuscript Grind

The necessary manuscript volume creates a “fair bump” in progression. To efficiently grind manuscripts:

  1. Maximize Capacity: Max out your kitten population using Huts and Log Houses to increase Catpower limits and production rate (for hunting furs).
  2. Increase Culture: Build as many Amphitheatres and Temples as reasonably possible, and buy all available culture and catpower bonuses from the Religion tab. Culture generating buildings like Amphitheatres, Academies, and Libraries also boost the culture storage cap, which is often constrained.
  3. Boost Crafting: Maximizing your Workshops is essential, as this provides a multiplicative bonus to all crafting operations, including manuscript creation.
  4. Kitten Allocation: A suggested method for grinding is to temporarily move all kittens to Hunters to generate a massive stockpile of Parchment (since Parchment creation should initially outpace culture consumption), then craft manuscripts whenever your Culture storage maxes out.

Persistence on Reset

Manuscripts are classified as Craftable Resources. They are generally lost upon reset, but they can be conditionally carried over if the player has Chronospheres and the Flux Condensator upgrade. Each Chronosphere preserves $1.5%* 100* \sqrt{X}$ of the resource, where $X$ is the amount before reset, meaning they carry over with diminishing returns.

In the accelerated, late-game reset loop, stocking up on crafted resources like manuscripts is essential for quickly getting back up to speed. For example, stocking 19.6k manuscripts is recommended for maximizing resource carryover using one Chronosphere.

item.title: Compendium

  • Next Tier Resource: Once Physics is researched, Compendiums become the resource used to craft Blueprints.

Metaphysics Upgrades (Codexes)

The importance of Compendium crafting is recognised in the permanent Metaphysics upgrade system:

  • Codex Logos: Costs 50 Paragon and specifically adds +25% to your craft ratio when crafting Compendia. It also multiplies all Compendium crafting by $\times 1.05$.
  • Codex Agrum: Costs 75 Paragon and further increases the Compendium craft multiplier to $\times 1.1$.
  • Codex Leviathanianus: Costs 75 Paragon and increases the Compendium cut-off limit by $5%$ per Transcendence tier.

While these Codex upgrades boost crafting efficiency, they are often considered low priority for newer players due to their high cost and small returns compared to the critical price ratio reduction upgrades.

For players executing quick runs designed to accumulate Paragon quickly, stockpiling a certain amount of Compendiums (e.g., 16.1k Compendia) before resetting with a Chronosphere and the Flux Condensator upgrade is recommended, as this crafted resource can be carried over to accelerate the next run. This allows players to skip the time-consuming process of crafting them immediately in the new run.

item.title: Blueprint
item.description:
Blueprints are a crucial Craftable Resource required for technological advancement and the construction of advanced industrial buildings in Kittens Game.

Here is a comprehensive overview of Blueprints:

Acquisition

Blueprints can be acquired through crafting or trade:

  1. Crafting:

    • Blueprints are crafted from 25 Compendium and 25,000 Science.
    • The capacity to craft Blueprints is unlocked after researching the Physics technology.
    • Crafting blueprints is considered to have an “incredibly steep production cost”, and the process is the same as crafting Manuscripts.
    • The process often requires mass conversion: first converting Furs into Parchment, then Parchment into Manuscripts, and finally Manuscripts into Compendiums before crafting the Blueprint.
    • The Metaphysics upgrade Codex Agrum reduces the cost growth ratio by adding +25% to your blueprint craft ratio and multiplying the blueprint craft multiplier by x1.05.

  2. Trading:

    • Any successful trade with other civilizations has a 10% chance of including one blueprint as an extra resource. This is a fixed rate that cannot be increased by other trade bonuses.
    • Trading is often the preferred initial method, as players are advised to “keep Trading with other civilizations until you luck out and get a Blueprints for free” due to their steep production cost.
    • Trading with Nagas can specifically boost Blueprint acquisition: Building Naga embassies increases the chance to get blueprints from Nagas by 0.25%, capping at 10% at 40 embassies. Once the maximum bonus is achieved, embassies over 40 improve the blueprint crafting ratio instead.

Cycles Numerology and Numeromancy Metaphysics. Certain cycles (Kairo, Cath, Piscine) boost the production of starcharts from space structures. The Kairo Cycle provides a large boost, increasing starchart income by 5x and increasing space beacon starchart production by +400%.

Starcharts are often considered a major roadblock in the progression towards the space phase of the game.

The Starchart is a critical mid-to-late-game special resource necessary for advancing space exploration, unlocking advanced trade methods, and progressing the technological tree.

Here is a detailed breakdown of its acquisition, production, and importance:

1. Acquisition and Production

Starcharts are unlocked after researching Astronomy. They are initially acquired through rare events, with later production managed through dedicated buildings and kitten jobs.

Method Mechanism/Source Details
Astronomical Events Observing rare events after building a Library. The base chance for an event is 0.25% every day. Each Observatory built increases this chance by an additive 0.2% per day. The event must be manually clicked, or it may automatically succeed with a 1% chance per Observatory.
Automation SETI Workshop Upgrade (unlocked by Electronics). This upgrade causes all astronomical events to succeed automatically and silently, instantly granting associated science and starcharts.
Buildings Observatories, Satellites, Research Vessels, and Space Beacons. Research Vessels produce 0.05 starcharts/sec, and Space Beacons produce 0.125 starcharts/sec. Satellites produce 0.005 starcharts/sec.
Kitten Jobs Scholar profession. The Astrophysicists Workshop upgrade allows Scholar kittens to produce +0.0005 starcharts/sec.
Trade Leviathans. Leviathans trade 250 Starchart (with a 50% chance) in exchange for 5000 Unobtainium.
Cycles Numerology and Numeromancy Metaphysics. Certain cycles (Kairo, Cath, Piscine) boost the production of starcharts from space structures. The Kairo Cycle provides a large boost, increasing starchart income by 5x and increasing space beacon starchart production by +400%.

2. Strategic Role and Progression Bottleneck

Starcharts are often considered a major roadblock in the progression towards the space phase of the game.

Key Uses:

  • Trade Ships: Starcharts are required for crafting Trade Ships, which are crucial for finding and trading with the Zebras to acquire Titanium. Crafting a Trade Ship costs 25 Starchart (this cost can be reduced by the Satellite Navigation upgrade).
  • Space Missions: They are required for all missions in the Space tab, which is unlocked by Rocketry. The costs escalate significantly: the initial Orbital Launch costs 250 Starchart, and the subsequent Moon Mission costs 500 Starchart. Later missions require thousands, such as the Kairo Mission (5000 Starchart) and Rorschach Mission (15,000 Starchart).
  • Advanced Structures: They are necessary for high-tier structures like the Space Beacon (25,000 Starchart) and the Orbital Array (2000 Starchart).
  • Workshop Upgrades: The Geodesy Workshop upgrade, which enables Geologists to find gold, requires 500 Starchart.

Mitigation Strategy:

  • To overcome the starchart bottleneck and obtain the necessary titanium, it is crucial to focus on Observatories immediately after unlocking Astronomy.
  • Metaphysics upgrades like Chronomancy and Astromancy are recommended because starchart production tends to lag, and these upgrades help increase the chance of astronomical events, accelerating the building of a large trade fleet.
  • In the late game, the most efficient method for starchart production is through Research Vessels, although acquiring the first vessel is costly (requiring 2000 total Starcharts for mission and building).

3. Challenge Mode Interactions

The production and necessity of Starcharts change dramatically when certain challenges are active:

  • Black Sky Challenge: This challenge specifically disables astronomical events. Furthermore, Research Vessels no longer produce starcharts in this challenge. However, the initial cost of the Orbital Launch mission is altered, and the starchart requirement is removed.
  • Iron Will Mode: In this challenging mode, astronomical events observed after building Libraries are the only initial source of Science. If the Iron Will mode is combined with the Black Sky Challenge, astrological events are fully disabled, removing one of the main sources of science.

Starcharts are one of the resources that may conditionally carry over on a reset if you have Chronospheres. Specifically, starcharts are included in the list of non-crafted resources preserved by Chronospheres. For a quick paragon farming run, players may stock up to 390k starcharts to carry over 5,850 starcharts (assuming one Chronosphere).

1. Acquisition and Trade

Titanium is initially acquired primarily through trade, though advanced structures provide domestic production later.

Trading with Zebras

The most important early source is through trading with Zebras, who are initially a Hostile civilisation (-30% attitude).

  • Trade Mechanism: Zebras sell Titanium in exchange for Slab (a craftable resource made from Minerals).
  • Scaling: The amount of titanium sold by Zebras is not affected by typical trading bonuses like those from Tradeposts. Instead, the amount of titanium they give is calculated as (0.03 * Trade Ships) + 1.5.
  • Prerequisite: To unlock Zebras for trade, you must first build at least one Trade Ship.
  • Policy Boost: The policy Zebra Relations: Appeasement improves relations with Zebras (as 15 extra Tradeposts) and grants a +15 tradeposts worth of trade ratio titanium sold (multiplicative).
  • Strategic Focus: The strategic goal in the mid-game is to build Observatories to generate Starcharts, which allow you to craft more Trade Ships, thereby accelerating the rate of titanium flow.

Domestic Production (Conversion)

Titanium can be produced domestically through industrial structures that convert other resources:

  • Calciners: Titanium is refined from oil and minerals by Calciners. A single Calciner produces +0.0005 Titanium per Tick. This production can be significantly boosted by upgrades like Oxidation (+285%) and Fluidized Reactors (+300%).
  • Smelters: After researching Nuclear Fission, the Nuclear Smelter upgrade allows Smelters to produce Titanium at a rate of 0.0015 per tick.
  • Policy Boost: The Communism policy provides a straight +25% production boost to iron, coal, and titanium.

2. Strategic Uses and Cost

Titanium is a heavily demanded resource for high-level buildings, workshop upgrades, and space travel.

Key Building Costs

Titanium is required for constructing advanced infrastructure and housing:

Building Titanium Cost Prerequisite/Context
Reactor 3500 Required for Nuclear Fission
Factory 2000 Unlocked by Mechanization
Hydro Plant 2500 Upgrade from Aqueduct; transition should wait until Titanium production is good
Accelerator 7500 Unlocked by Particle Physics
Mansion 25 High-tier housing
Cryostation 7500 (in cost of Cryostation) Advanced storage facility

Upgrades and Progression

Titanium is needed to progress through the housing and crafting technology tree:

  • Housing Upgrades: The core progression upgrade Concrete Huts requires 3000 Titanium, and the later Unobtainium Huts requires 15,000 Titanium.
  • Workshop Upgrades: Titanium is needed for efficiency upgrades such as Titanium Saw and Titanium Axe, and advanced industrial upgrades like Factory Logistics.
  • Space Missions: Titanium is a required resource for several space missions, including the Moon Mission (5000 Titanium) and Dune Mission (7000 Titanium).
  • Uranium Acquisition: Dragons buy Titanium (250 units) and sell Uranium.

3. Storage and Capacity

Titanium has a default initial storage capacity of 2 units. This limit must be increased via storage buildings:

  • Harbours increase storage by +50 Titanium.
  • Moon Bases increase storage by +1250 Titanium.
  • Cryostations increase storage by +7500 Titanium.
  • Accelerators with the Energy Rifts upgrade provide a substantial storage boost, including +750 Titanium.
  • Sunforges also improve storage capacity for base metals, including titanium, by +1% each.

In the mid-game, Titanium storage may become capped quickly due to high rates of trade, requiring players to continuously build more storage structures and trade with Dragons to convert excess Titanium into Uranium.

Uses and Upgrades

Uranium is essential for progressing into the space and atomic eras of the game:

  • Refining Unobtainium: Uranium is refined into Unobtainium by a Lunar Outpost [1, 6]. This is a critical step for unlocking Metaphysics [6, 12].
  • Fueling Reactors: Uranium is consumed by the Reactor building at a rate of $0.001$ per tick to generate energy [13]. The Enriched Uranium upgrade reduces this consumption by 25% [9, 13].
  • Refining Thorium: Uranium is used to craft Thorium at a rate of 250 Uranium per unit of Thorium [14]. This is unlocked by the Thorium science [15].
  • Advanced Buildings: Uranium is a cost component for several advanced buildings, including the Accelerator (25 Uranium) [5] and the Reactor (25 Blueprints, 50 Concrete, 5,000 Plate, and 3,500 Titanium) [13].
  • Workshop Upgrades: Uranium is required for several high-tier upgrades, such as:
    • Energy Rifts (from Accelerators) [16].
    • Stasis Chambers [16].
    • Void Energy [16].
    • Nuclear Plants [8].
    • Augmentations [9].

Storage Capacity

The default maximum storage capacity for Uranium is 250 [17].

  • This capacity is mainly increased by building Reactors, as each Reactor increases the maximum Uranium storage by +250 [13].
  • The Accelerator building is also a key component for storage upgrades, as Accelerators, with the Energy Rifts upgrade, provide substantial storage capacity for common resources, including Uranium [16].

Uranium represents a bottleneck resource in the mid-to-late game [18]. Its acquisition and refinement pathway is critical because Unobtainium, the resource it creates, is necessary to unlock the powerful and permanent upgrades found in the Metaphysics system [6, 19].

What Produces Uranium

Uranium, a critical resource in the later stages of the game, is primarily acquired through three methods: trading with the Dragons, production via upgraded Quarries, and refinement using Accelerators.

Here is a breakdown of what produces or provides Uranium:

1. Production via Buildings and Upgrades

Uranium can be produced directly using advanced buildings and upgrades:

  • Quarry (with Orbital Geodesy): Quarries will provide a small amount of uranium once the Orbital Geodesy upgrade is purchased [1, 2]. Quarries produce uranium at a rate of 0.0005 per tick.
    • Orbital Geodesy requires Satellites technology and costs 150,000 Science, 1,000 Alloy, and 35,000 Oil.
  • Accelerator: This building refines titanium into uranium. Accelerators produce 0.0025 uranium per tick (or 0.0125 per second) [3, 4].
    • The Accelerator building is unlocked by researching the Particle Physics science [3, 5]. It costs 7,500 Titanium, 125 Concrete, and 25 Uranium.
  • Planet Cracker: Uranium is produced by the Planet Cracker structure [1, 6]. This structure’s output is affected by the Dune cycle, which can increase its uranium output by +10% [7].
  • Reactor (Consumption Reduction): While Reactors consume Uranium [8], the Enriched Uranium upgrade reduces this consumption by 25% and also provides a +25% uranium production bonus that applies only to Quarries [9].

2. Acquisition via Trade

The most straightforward way to initially acquire Uranium is through trade:

  • Dragons: Uranium can be bought from the Dragons civilization, in exchange for Titanium.
    • Dragons sell 1 Uranium and the trade has a 95% chance of success (reaching 100% chance with 6 Embassy levels) [10, 11].
    • Dragons are unlocked after researching Nuclear Fission [12].

3. Production Boosts

Uranium production can be boosted by:

  • Cycles (Dune): The Dune cycle doubles Uranium income when the Numerology metaphysics upgrade is researched [7].
  • Enriched Uranium: This Workshop upgrade increases Uranium production by +25% (but only applies to Quarries) [9].
  • Planet Busters: This upgrade doubles the output of the Planet Cracker structure [13].

Uranium is an important resource, particularly in the later stages of the game, as it is needed to refine Unobtainium via a Lunar Outpost [1, 4].

  • Refining into Relics: 25 Time Crystals can be refined into 1 Relic . Relics are necessary for buying Cryptotheology buildings like the Black Obelisk and Black Nexus .
  • Time and Void Science: TCs are prerequisites for key late-game technologies:
    • Chronophysics: Costs 5 Time Crystals.
    • Tachyon Theory: Costs 25 Time Crystals and 1 Relic.
    • Void Space: Costs 30 Time Crystals and 100 Void.
    • Paradox Theory: Costs 40 Time Crystals and 250 Void.
  • Time Manipulation and Antimatter: Time Crystals are integral to the Chronoforge system (unlocked by Tachyon Theory).
    • They are combusted in the Chrono Furnace to advance the year. Shattering TCs is done to skip time, triggering Antimatter gain from Sunlifters faster.
    • Shattering TCs is also required to reach the goal of the 1000 Years Challenge.
  • Advanced Structures and Upgrades: TCs are components for various high-tier structures and workshop upgrades:
    • Chronosphere: Costs 1 Time Crystal, among other resources, and is a prerequisite for generating Void and Temporal Flux [14, 21].
    • Flux Condensator: Requires 5 Time Crystals and is crucial for preserving a fraction of crafted resources across resets via Chronospheres.
    • Stasis Chambers (1 TC) and Void Energy (2 TCs) are upgrades for Accelerators.
  • Zebra Crafting: Time Crystals are also needed to craft Bloodstone (5K TCs and 10K Relics), which is used to craft T-Mythril.

Strategic Significance

Time Crystals play a unique role in game persistence and efficiency:

  • Reset Retention: The Metaphysics upgrade Anachronomancy (Cost: 125 Paragon) ensures that Time Crystals and the Chronophysics technology are saved across resets. This capability is critical for accelerating future runs. quick paragon farming runs
  • Engine Goal: Due to their importance in resets and late-game systems (Relics/Void), players aim to build up a large stockpile (20-30K TCs) to acquire upgrades like Resource Retrieval immediately after a reset, eliminating the slow initial grind for them.
  • Challenging Use: The 1000 Years Challenge is unlocked by shattering a Time Crystal and requires constant shattering (and associated TC costs) to advance the game’s calendar to Year 1000.

Time Crystals act as the key to temporal mechanics in Kittens Game. If Unobtainium is the material that unlocks space, Time Crystals are the resource that unlocks control over the flow of time itself, allowing kittens to either speed up their civilization or carry advantages across dimensional resets.

Acquisition

Relics are not produced by buildings or jobs but must be acquired through late-game conversion, trade, or specialized structures:

  1. Refining Time Crystals (Crafting): You can refine 25 Time Crystals to receive 1 Relic. This action requires having at least 25 Time Crystals.
  2. Trade (Leviathans): Relics can be bought from the Leviathans. Leviathans buy 5,000 Unobtainium and sell 1 Relic with a 5% chance of success. Leviathans are unlocked after building a Black Pyramid.
  3. Relic Station (Production): The Relic Station building (unlocked by the Cryptotheology science and purchased with 5,000 Antimatter and 100 Eludium) generates $0.01$ relic per day. Relic production from the Relic Station scales based on Antimatter storage, meaning production is reduced proportionally if maximum Antimatter storage is less than 5,000.
  4. Black Nexus Boost: The production from Space Beacons upgraded with Relic Station is improved by the Black Nexus Cryptotheology upgrade, which produces $0.01* (1 + (Black Pyramid * Black Nexus/10))$ relics per day.

Primary Uses and Upgrades

Relics are the required resource for purchasing most buildings and upgrades within the Cryptotheology system, which unlocks advanced mechanics and bonuses:

  • Technology Advancement: Relics are necessary for key high-tier sciences:
    • Tachyon Theory: Costs 1 Relic and 750K Science .
    • Cryptotheology: Costs 5 Relics and 650K Science.
    • Antimatter: Costs 1 Relic and 500K Science.
    • Terraformation: Costs 5 Relics and 750K Science.
    • Quantum Cryptography: Costs 1024 Relics and 1.25M Science.
  • Cryptotheology Buildings: Relics are spent to purchase permanent prestige buildings:
    • Black Obelisk: Costs 100 Relics.
    • Black Nexus: Costs 5,000 Relics.
    • Blazar: Costs 50,000 Relics and is required to reach Transcendence Tier 15.
    • Event Horizon: Costs 25,000 Relics and increases global resource storage ratio by 10%.
    • Holy Genocide: Costs 100,000 Relics and unlocks the Post Apocalypse challenge.
  • Chronoforge: Relics are a cost component for the Chronoforge upgrade (5 Relics), which is necessary for time manipulation features and the Shatter Engine.
  • Pacts: Pacts are purchased for 100 Relics each.

Strategic Role (Relic Engines)

Obtaining Relics is the primary focus of the mid-game. Players develop specialized strategies, or “engines,” to increase relic flow:

  1. Type 0 Engine (Leviathan Trade): Relies on trading 5,000 Unobtainium to Leviathans for relics. This can be optimized by using the Chronoforge to skip non-Redmoon cycles (which boost Unobtainium production) .
  2. Type 1 Engine (Relic Stations): Involves mass-producing Space Beacons and the Relic Station upgrade, enhancing production with Black Nexus and AI Cores.
  3. Type 2 Engine (Shatter Engine): Requires investing vast amounts of Time Crystals into Resource Retrieval to reach a point where shattering a single Time Crystal yields enough Unobtainium to immediately trade with Leviathans for multiple new Time Crystals, allowing for rapid Time Crystal refinement into Relics.

Relics are the final currency gate before the ultimate goal of maximizing Antimatter and Void resources to prepare for the End Game push for Infinity.

Strategic Uses

Gold is a critical bottleneck for mid-game progression due to its diverse applications:

  • Trade: Each trade transaction with civilizations like the Lizards, Sharks, or Zebras typically costs 1 unit of gold.
  • Religion: Gold is a required component for building Temples and purchasing many Order of the Sun upgrades, such as Solar Revolution, Golden Spire, and Sun Altar.
  • Village Infrastructure: It is necessary for constructing Tradeposts (which improve trade and happiness) and Mints (which automate the gathering of furs and ivory).
  • Leadership: Promoting a kitten to a higher rank requires both experience and gold. Higher-ranked leaders provide significant production bonuses, especially if the Monarchy or Republic policies are enacted.

Strategic Gold Cap Benchmarks

Expanding gold storage is critical for scientific and religious progression:

  • Solar Revolution: Requires a gold cap of 500.
  • Apocrypha: Requires a gold cap of 5,000.
  • Transcendence: Requires a gold cap of 7,500.
  • Leadership Promotions: Higher ranks for your kitten leaders require significant gold amounts, ranging from 25 to 200+ gold.

Policies and Efficiency

Several government and foreign policies directly impact your gold economy:

  • Liberalism: This policy is highly valued as it reduces all gold costs by 20% and improves trade relations.
  • Zebra Relations (Appeasement): While this policy improves titanium trade, it imposes a -5% penalty to gold income.
  • Monarchy: This policy doubles the power of your leader’s trait but consumes 10% of your gold production as upkeep for the royal court.

The initial storage limit for Gold is 10 units. This capacity can be increased through the construction of specific storage buildings, as well as production buildings that feature storage benefits, such as the Mint [1, 2].

Here are the ways to increase your maximum Gold storage:

1. Dedicated Buildings and Upgrades

Several buildings directly contribute to your maximum Gold capacity:

  • Mint: The Mint building increases your Max Gold by +100. Mints are unlocked by researching Architecture and are constructed using 5,000 Minerals, 200 Plate, and 500 Gold. Building more Mints is suggested as a method to increase your Gold storage limit.
  • Barn: The Barn, unlocked by Agriculture, provides a base increase of +10 Max Gold [1, 5].
  • Warehouse: The Warehouse, unlocked by Construction, provides a base increase of +5 Max Gold.
  • Harbour: The Harbour, unlocked by Navigation, provides a base increase of +25 Max Gold.
  • Sky Palace: The Sky Palace, a religious building, improves gold storage by +1%.

2. Storage Upgrades

Various Workshop upgrades applied to storage buildings will further increase the Gold capacity of Mints, Warehouses, and Harbours:

  • Reinforced Warehouses: Increases the maximum limit for several resources, including Gold, from Warehouses, Barns, Harbors, and Mints by +25% [7]. This upgrade is unlocked by Steel [7, 8].
  • Titanium Warehouses: Increases Gold capacity from the specified storage buildings by +50% [4, 7].
  • Alloy Warehouses: Increases Gold capacity from the specified storage buildings by +45% [7].
  • Concrete Pillars: Increases Gold capacity from the specified storage buildings by +5% [7].
  • Concrete Warehouses: Increases Gold capacity from the specified storage buildings by +35% [7].
  • Storage Bunkers: Increases Gold capacity from the specified storage buildings by +20%. This upgrade is unlocked by Exogeology [7, 9].

3. Advanced Mechanisms

Late-game advanced production and prestige mechanics also influence Gold capacity:

  • Paragon: High levels of Paragon (gained by resetting with more than 70 kittens) improve resource caps, and this effect on storage never diminishes [10, 11].
  • Accelerator Upgrades: Advanced Accelerator Workshop upgrades, associated with pocket dimensions, also increase the maximum capacity of Gold:
    • Energy Rifts (Requires Dimensional Physics) [12].
    • Stasis Chambers (Requires Chronophysics) increases max Gold from Accelerators by +95% [12].
    • Void Energy (Requires Stasis Chambers) increases max Gold from Accelerators by +75% [12].
    • Dark Energy (Requires Void Energy) increases max Gold from Accelerators by +250% [12].
    • Tachyon Accelerators (Requires Tachyon Theory) increases max Gold from Accelerators by +500% [12].
  • Event Horizon: This Cryptotheology upgrade, available at Transcendence-Tier 7, increases the global resource storage ratio by +10% [13].

Strategic Importance

Increasing Gold storage is necessary because Gold is used extensively:

  • Trading: Gold is required for trading with civilizations [14], and the Isolationism policy reduces the Gold cost per trade by 1 [15].

  • Purpose: Plate is required for advanced construction in the early and mid-game, particularly for buildings like Harbours.

2. Supporting Iron Production (The Prerequisite)

Since Plate production is capped by your Iron supply, effective production requires robust Iron generation, which is achieved through refining and trade:

  • Smelters: Iron is refined from wood and minerals using Smelters. Smelters unlock after researching Metal Working.
  • Calciners: Iron can also be refined using Calciners from oil and minerals.
  • Upgrades: Several Workshop upgrades boost Iron production from these buildings:
    • Electrolytic Smelting increases Smelter output of iron (and coal) by +95%.
    • Fluidized Reactors boost Calciner output by +100% more iron.
    • Oxidation increases Calciner iron production by +95%.
    • The Rotary Kiln also provides a +75% increase to Calciner iron output.
  • Policy/: The Communism policy grants a +25% increase to iron production. The Rationality policy grants a +5% iron production bonus.
  • Trade: Iron can be acquired directly by trading with other races. For example, Griffins sell Iron for Wood, and Zebras sell Iron for Slab.

3. Automated Conversion and Trade Acquisition

  • Automation: The Pneumatic Press Workshop upgrade, unlocked via Physics, allows Workshop Automation to automatically convert iron to plates when iron resources are near their capacity limit.
  • Trade Acquisition: Plate can be acquired through trade with Zebras. Zebras sell Plate (2 units per trade, with a 65% chance) in exchange for 50 Slab. Building Embassies increases the chance of receiving plates from Zebras, reaching 100% chance at Embassy level 54.

4. Uses of Plate

Plate is crucial for further expanding infrastructure and developing advanced resources:

  • Storage: Plate is needed to build a Harbour (75 Plate), a storage building essential for increasing capacity for Catnip, Wood, Minerals, and Iron, among others.
  • Culture/Gold: Plate is required for Temples (15 Plate) and Mints (200 Plate). Mints increase gold storage and produce rare resources.
  • High-Tier Structures: Significant amounts of Plate are needed for Reactors (5000 Plate) and Factories (2500 Plate).
  • Late-Game Crafting: Plate is an input for crafting Megaliths (5 Plate).

Plate serves as an early example of vertical production integration in the game, where continuous management of raw resources (Wood, Minerals) is required to ensure a steady supply of an intermediary resource (Iron) which is then crafted into Plate for infrastructure expansion.

  • Stained Glass: This upgrade (which costs 500 Faith and 250 Gold, and requires 750 Worship) enhances Temple functionality by increasing their culture output by +0.05 Culture per Tick. This bonus increases by an additional +0.05 for each subsequent level purchased using Transcendence.
  • Basilica: This upgrade, available after accumulating 10,000 Worship, increases Temple culture per tick by +0.2.
  • Mysticism Policy: This policy provides a +5% culture and faith production bonus.
  • Cultural Exchange Policy: This policy grants a +5% culture income bonus.
  • Yarn Cycle: If Numeromancy is researched, holding a festival during the Yarn cycle grants a Culture income x2 bonus.

Like other special resources, Culture production benefits from Paragon and Religion production boosts.

Usage and Progression

Culture is used exclusively in the Workshop tab to craft Manuscripts.

  1. Crafting Manuscripts: To craft one Manuscript, you typically require 25 Parchment and 400 Culture. This cost can be reduced if you adopt the Tradition Policy, which reduces the cost to 20 Parchment and 300 Culture.
  2. Unlocking Advanced Tech: Manuscripts are vital for unlocking mid-game sciences:
    • Theology requires 20,000 Science and 35 Manuscripts.
    • Astronomy requires 28,000 Science and 65 Manuscripts.

The sources highlight that reaching the Theology science is gated by the steep requirement of needing to create Manuscripts using Parchment and Culture, a resource that accumulates slowly at first.

Storage Capacity

Culture is a capped resource, with an initial storage capacity of 100. Expanding this limit is necessary for accumulating enough culture to craft expensive manuscripts.

Maximum Culture capacity is increased by buildings and upgrades:

  • Library: +10 max culture.
  • Academy: +25 max culture.
  • Amphitheatre: +50 max culture.
  • Chapel: +200 max culture.

  • Basilica (Temple upgrade): +125 max culture to Temples, increasing by +50 per additional level via Transcendence.

  • Broadcast Tower (Amphitheatre upgrade): Max Culture + (300 multiplied by the Energy Surplus Ratio).
  • Unicorn Graveyard (Religious building): Increases maximum culture by +1% per Ziggurat.
  • Codex Logos (Metaphysics upgrade): Increases the Manuscript craft multiplier, which grants a minor bonus to maximum culture (with diminishing returns).

Accumulating enough Culture capacity is also necessary to interact with certain trade partners, as the Nagas are unlocked when you reach a 1500 Culture cap.

To progress through the initial difficulty of Culture accumulation, many players focus on building Amphitheatres and Temples and maximize their ability to hunt for Furs (which are refined into Parchment) to ensure they can sustain Manuscript production.

The default storage capacity for antimatter is 100 units. Expanding this cap is mandatory for high-level progression:

  • Containment Chambers: Constructed in the Kairo system, these provide +100 max antimatter each, but consume a heavy 50 Watts of energy.
  • Heatsinks: These increase the storage effectiveness of Containment Chambers by +2% per building.
  • The 5,000 Cap Goal: A major strategic milestone is reaching a 5,000 unit capacity, which is the cost of a Relic Station. To achieve this, a typical configuration requires approximately 34 Heatsinks and 29 Containment Chambers, supported by significant Paragon levels. If your maximum antimatter is below 5,000, your relic production efficiency is reduced proportionally.

Primary Uses

Antimatter is essential for transitioning into the endgame “Relic Engine” and optimizing space travel:

  • Relic Era Infrastructure: It is the core requirement for Relic Stations (5,000 AM) and Space Beacons (50 AM), which automate the generation of Relics.
  • Quantum Computing: Entanglement Stations, which generate hashes for cryptographical attacks on the elders, cost 5,250 AM.
  • AI and Automation: It is required to build AI Cores (125 AM) and purchase the Machine Learning upgrade (125 AM).
  • Space Upgrades: Advanced space missions and structures depend on it, including Terraforming Stations (25 AM), Tectonics (500 AM), and Antimatter Drives (125 AM).
  • Reactor Enhancements: It is used to upgrade standard infrastructure, such as Advanced AM Reactors (1,750 AM) and Void Reactors (2,500 AM).

Strategic Considerations

During the late game, players often engage in a “Seed Run”—a very long game session focused specifically on maximizing energy and containment to build a massive antimatter and void stockpile. Once the cap is high enough, you can perform Positive Resets with 70+ Chronospheres to exponentially grow your antimatter reserves across subsequent runs. To maximize production during these loops, players often turn off Thorium Reactors except when actively time-skipping to ensure the energy surplus remains positive for antimatter generation.

2. Acquisition and Production

Alicorns are not produced by standard jobs or early buildings; they are acquired through late-game religious structures and rare events:

  • Sky Palaces: This religious building, which requires Tears, Ivory, and Megalith to construct, is the main way to gain Alicorns [3].
    • Building a Sky Palace enables a random event that grants one Alicorn, and each palace increases the frequency of this event by $0.01%$ per game-day [3].
    • Sky Palaces also passively produce $0.00002$ alicorns per tick ($0.08$ per year) [3].
  • Unicorn Utopia: This subsequent unicorn religious upgrade improves alicorn summon chance by $0.015%$ per game-day and increases passive production to $0.000025$ alicorns per tick [4].
  • Pacifism Challenge Reward: Completing the Pacifism challenge provides an increasing reward, including a $+10%$ Alicorn chance per completion (up to $120%$) and a $10%$ increase to Alicorn per tick production (with no diminishing returns) [5].

3. Primary Uses and Conversion

Alicorns are primarily consumed to generate Time Crystals (TC), a valuable prestige resource:

  • Sacrifice for Time Crystals: You can Sacrifice 25 Alicorns to receive 1 Time Crystal [6].
    • The conversion ratio is improved by the religious upgrades Unicorn Utopia (+5%) and Sunspire (+10%) [4, 6].
    • The act is described as “Banish the alicorns to the Bloodmoon” [6].
  • Resource Retrieval Strategy: In the end game, acquiring enough levels of the Resource Retrieval upgrade means shattering a Time Crystal will yield enough unobtainium and alicorns to allow the player to Civilisations/sacrifice immediately for new Time Crystals, sustaining the flow of this resource [7].

4. Consumption and Corruption

Alicorns are consumed or corrupted in three ways:

  • Necrocorn Corruption: The religious building Marker starts a process that slowly changes alicorns into Necrocorns [1, 8].
  • Unicorn Necropolis: The Unicorn Necropolis building, an advanced religious structure, requires 100 Alicorn (along with Necrocorn, Megalith, and Void) [9].
  • Ivory Temple Consumption: The Ivory Temple, a building related to Zebras, consumes $0.00002$ alicorns per tick while converting Ivory to Minerals [10].

In terms of strategy, it is advised to conserve your alicorn supply until the “last moment” to maximize the Time Crystal conversion ratio, particularly during a final run before a reset [11].

item.description:
Coal is a Common Resource in Kittens Game that is essential for progressing into the industrial phase of the game.

Here is a comprehensive overview of how Coal is produced, its strategic importance, and its consumption:

Acquisition and Production

Coal production is unlocked after researching the Steel technology. Once unlocked, Coal can be generated in several ways:

  1. Mines (Deep Mining Upgrade): The Deep Mining upgrade, unlocked by Steel, allows Mines to produce Coal.

    • Mines produce Coal at a rate of 0.003 Coal per tick (0.015 per second).
    • This upgrade requires 5,000 Science, 1,200 Iron, and 50 Beam.

  2. Smelters (Coal Furnace Upgrade): The Coal Furnace upgrade, also unlocked by Steel, enables Smelters to produce Coal.

    • Smelters produce Coal at a rate of 0.005 Coal per tick (0.025 per second) while burning wood.
    • This upgrade costs 5,000 Science, 5,000 Minerals, 2,000 Iron, and 35 Beam.

    • The Mining Drill upgrade further boosts Geologist Coal production by 0.01 Coal per tick (0.05/sec).
    • The Unobtainium Drill upgrade provides an additional boost of 0.015 Coal per tick (0.075/sec).

  4. Quarries: The Quarry building, unlocked by Geology, automatically produces Coal at a rate of 0.015 Coal per tick.

  5. Trading (Spiders): Coal can be acquired by trading Scaffolds with Spiders.

    • Trade with Spiders for Coal is optimally performed during Autumn (+15% amount modifier).

Eludium is required for constructing the highest tier of housing and for high-level upgrades:

  • Eludium Huts (Housing): The Eludium Huts upgrade reduces the price ratio of Huts by 10% [5, 6]. To purchase this upgrade, you need 275K Science and 125 Eludium [3, 6].
  • Workshop Upgrades: Eludium is necessary for numerous advanced Workshop upgrades, often enhancing high-tier buildings:
    • Dark Energy: Increases Max Catnip, Wood, Minerals, Coal, Iron, Titanium, and Gold storage from Accelerators by +250% [6].
    • Tachyon Accelerators: Increases the same Accelerator storage capacities by +500% [6].
    • Tachyon Drive: A rocket engine that sets space travel speed to 50 (or 75 combined with Antimatter Drive) [7].
    • Cryocomputing: Reduces Data Center energy consumption from 2Wt to 1Wt [8].
    • Quantum Dot Cells: Improves Solar Farm energy production by +15% in winter and +30% in spring and autumn [6].
    • Antimatter Fission/Reactors/Drive: Required for various Antimatter-related upgrades [8, 9].
    • Chronoengineers: Improves Engineer effectiveness and allows them to work during time skips [7].
  • Space Structures: Eludium is used in the construction of the Spaceport [10].
  • Cryptotheology: Eludium is a cost component for advanced Cryptotheology buildings such as the Relic Station [8].

Strategic Context

The process of acquiring Eludium defines a major phase of the game progression, known as the Eludium Era.

  • This era requires increasing the Unobtainium Production Rate to a reasonable level, primarily through Planet Crackers (to generate Uranium) and Lunar Outposts (to convert Uranium to Unobtainium) [11].
  • Achieving Eludium Huts is considered the next major checkpoint after Concrete Huts [12, 13]. Once Eludium Huts are built, the player is considered ready for the subsequent Unicorn/Time Crystal Era, provided the Unobtainium generation rate is high enough (around 1 Unobtainium per second or 1,100 Paragon plus the Renaissance upgrade) [14].

Analogy: If Alloy is the steel frame of a skyscraper, and Unobtainium is the unique, high-strength glass that allows it to reach impossible heights, then Eludium is the final, specialized rivet that binds them together, enabling construction of structures (like Eludium Huts) that define the architectural apex of the kitten civilization.

Researching Exogeology unlocks several crucial elements and leads directly to the next phase of high-tier crafting:

  • Housing Upgrade: It unlocks the Unobtainium Huts upgrade. This upgrade requires 200K Science, 350 Unobtainium, and 15K Titanium, and reduces the Hut price ratio by 25%.
  • Storage and Production Upgrades: It unlocks several specialized Workshop upgrades:
    • Unobtainium Reflectors: These improve telescope reflectors, increasing the maximum science bonus gained from Observatories by an additional 2% per Observatory.
    • Unobtainium Drill: This improves the effectiveness of Geologists.
    • Hydro Plant Turbines: This upgrade makes Hydro Plants 15% more effective (increasing energy output from 5 Wt to 5.75 Wt).
    • Storage Bunkers: This is a vital storage upgrade that increases the maximum storage limit for wood, minerals, coal, iron, gold, and titanium from Warehouses, Barns, Harbors, and Mints by 20%. The storage bunkers upgrade requires 25K Science, 500 Unobtainium, and 1250 Concrete.

3. Strategic Importance (The Unobtainium Era)

Exogeology marks the beginning of the “Unobtainium Era” and is a step towards the “Eludium Era” [6, 7].

  • Storage Bottleneck: Acquiring the Storage Bunkers upgrade, which Exogeology unlocks, is recommended once you reach 500 Unobtainium capacity [8]. This helps address storage limits, which are a major bottleneck in the game [9, 10].
  • Late-Game Progression: After achieving Concrete Huts (unlocked by Mechanization) [11], players should aim for Unobtainium Huts, which are unlocked by Exogeology, before attempting to reset the game, as this marks a major population and storage milestone [12].
  • Eludium Goal: The ultimate goal after Exogeology is to research Exometallurgy to craft Eludium. This typically requires significant Unobtainium storage (e.g., 1000 Unobtainium capacity via multiple Moon Bases or a Cryostation) to reach the capacity needed for Eludium Huts [7].

If you are following the recommended progression path, you should continue resetting once you can reach the Unobtainium Huts until you have acquired the Renaissance Metaphysics upgrade (750 Paragon), which makes reaching Unobtainium Huts easier in subsequent runs [7].

item.title: Gigaflops
item.description:
Gigaflops is the raw computational throughput unit generated by AI Cores. It measures computational work per second and directly governs how fast your AI Level (G-Level) increases toward the AI Apocalypse.

How Gigaflops Work

  • Source: Every powered AI Core produces Gigaflops.

  • Energy Demand: AI Cores consume large amounts of electricity (scaling per core). If your energy grid enters a brownout, Gigaflop output drops or halts completely.

  • Conversion to AI Level: Gigaflops act like an experience bar. When cumulative Gigaflops reach a dynamic capacity threshold, your AI Level increases by 1, resetting the Gigaflop counter to fill the next tier.

  • Scaling Threshold: The Gigaflop capacity required to reach the next AI Level scales exponentially:

    {Required Gigaflops} = {Base} * (1 + {AI Level})^{2 to 3}

As Gigaflops accumulate and elevate your AI Level, the AI system becomes increasingly dangerous:

  3. Resetting the Counter: Resetting your game (or triggering specific late-game containment protocols) clears the accumulated AI Level back to zero.

Acquisition and Persistence

Paragon is primarily acquired by reaching a certain population level before resetting the game:

  • You gain Paragon upon reset if you have more than 70 kittens [3, 4].
  • The reward is one point per kitten over 70.
  • Paragon is also gained at a passive rate of +1 for every 1,000 years that pass in the game.
  • Paragon, along with burned paragon, carries over after every game reset.

Primary Purpose: The Metaphysics System

Paragon is the currency used to purchase permanent enhancements in the Metaphysics tab. The Metaphysics system itself must be researched again each run, but the purchased upgrades persist.

The central function of Metaphysics upgrades is to reduce the cost growth of buildings, often referred to as price ratio reduction, allowing players to buy “lots more stuff” [6-8]. This reduction only applies to buildings in the Bonfire tab.

Key Metaphysics upgrades and their Paragon costs include:

Upgrade Category Upgrade Name Paragon Cost Purpose/Effect
Price Ratio Reduction Enlightenment 5 Reduces all price ratios by 1%.
Golden Ratio 50 [9] Reduces price ratios by approximately 1.618% [9].
Divine Proportion 100 [10] Reduces price ratios by approximately 1.777% [10].
Vitruvian Feline 250 [10] Reduces price ratios by 2% [10].
Renaissance 750 [10] Reduces price ratios by 2.25% [10].
QoL/Progression Diplomacy 5 [10] Races are discovered earlier and with better standing [10].
Anachronomancy 125 [11] Saves Time Crystals and Chronophysics technology across resets [11].
Megalomania 10 [9] Unlocks late-game Unicorn mechanics (Markers and Black Pyramids) [9].
Adjustment Bureau 5 [12] Unlocks Challenges [12, 13].

Effects on Production and Storage

Paragon provides substantial, permanent boosts to your civilization:

  • Production Boost: Paragon generally increases production rates [2, 14]. However, the production benefit experiences diminishing returns. Once a player reaches about 150 Paragon, the effectiveness starts to decrease. For example, 150 Paragon provides a 150% production increase, but 400 Paragon only increases it to 190%.
  • Storage Boost: Paragon increases resource storage capacity, and this effect never diminishes [15]. High levels of Paragon are crucial for bypassing major storage bottlenecks [15]. Specifically, Paragon boosts Moon Bases and Cryostations storage by 0.1% per Paragon [16].
  • Space Production: It is noted that Paragon has no effect on the production of space structures [17].

The Production Bonus Threshold

The global production bonus increases linearly for your first 150 Paragon (1 point = +1% production) After this point, each additional point of Paragon provides progressively less production value:

  • 150 Paragon: +150% productivity bonus
  • 200 Paragon: +175% productivity bonus
  • 400 Paragon: +190% productivity bonus

Plateau: Once you reach approximately 300 normal Paragon, additional points provide negligible increases to your production rates.

The Exception: Storage Capacity Unlike the production bonus, the effectiveness of Paragon on storage never diminishes. Each point of Paragon provides a permanent +0.1% bonus to resource storage capacity. This makes high levels of Paragon (into the thousands or millions) essential for the late-game “Chrono-resets,” where breaking through massive Unobtainium storage caps is the primary bottleneck.

Burned Paragon

Players have the option to “burn” Paragon, which is useful for specialized runs and stacking bonuses [4, 18]:

  • Effectiveness: Burned Paragon has half the effectiveness of regular Paragon, but it stacks with regular Paragon. The production gain from the first 75 burned Paragon gives a 1% production gain and is additive to the normal Paragon bonus [19].
  • Strategy: It is suggested that players aiming for maximum efficiency burn Paragon once they reach around 400 regular Paragon [19]. The boost from burned Paragon is particularly important in the Iron Will challenge mode, where the Metaphysics price ratio upgrades are still beneficial [18].

End Game Scaling

In the very late game, Paragon scaling can be improved through high-cost Metaphysics upgrades called Sefirot metas (e.g., Malkuth, Yesod, Hod, etc.) [20]. These upgrades cost between 500 Paragon (Malkuth) and 60,000 Paragon (Keter) [12, 21]. Each Sefirot meta improves Paragon effect and scaling by 5% [12, 21].

For players pursuing extreme end-game goals, specific strategies exist for rapid Paragon generation, such as the “cryo engine” method, which can yield up to 15 million Paragon per day [22].

You accumulate paragon primarily through two mechanisms: resetting your game based on your kitten population, and through the passage of time [5, 6].

Primary Methods of Accumulation

  1. Resetting with Kittens: Paragon is gained when you reset the game if you have more than 70 kittens [5-7]. You earn one paragon point for every kitten beyond the initial 70 [7].

    • Resetting the game is considered the fifth step in the basic gameplay cycle, occurring when progress becomes too slow.
    • For your first reset, it is recommended to aim for 130 or more kittens to secure at least 60 paragon [8]. Subsequent runs aim for higher kitten counts, such as 170+ for 100 paragon, or 220+ for 150 paragon [8].

  2. Time Passage: You are granted +1 paragon for every 1,000 years that pass in the game.

Advanced and End-Game Accumulation

In the later stages of the game, players utilize highly efficient methods to generate massive amounts of paragon:

  • Mass Shatterings (Time Skipping): You can gain paragon rapidly by advancing time using Time Crystals (TCs) and the Chronoforge or Time Boilers. This method yields 1 paragon for every thousand years skipped [9]. This technique is sometimes referred to as the “Shatter Engine” [9, 10].
  • The Holy Genocide Upgrade: Once you reach Transcendence-Tier 25 and purchase the Holy Genocide cryptotheology upgrade, resetting grants a +2% increase in paragon gained per kitten [11].
  • The Cryo Engine: A late-game technique involving resetting while possessing 3,000 Cryochambers is theorised to yield approximately 15 million paragon per day [12].
  • Mass Kitten Accumulation: Utilizing Festivals, especially when combined with the Terraformation mission upgrade “Tempus Fugit” (not explicitly detailed how it works with festivals in the source, but mentioned in context), to rapidly grow a large kitten population (e.g., ~60,000 kittens) can yield up to 120,000 paragon per day [9].

Once accumulated, paragon is used to purchase Metaphysics upgrades such as the price ratio reduction upgrades (e.g., Enlightenment, Golden Ratio, Divine Proportion, Vitruvian Feline, and Renaissance), which make buildings cheaper in future runs [2, 13-15].

Analogy: Accumulating paragon is like cashing in your retirement savings (your current civilization) to gain a permanent, compounding financial head start (Metaphysics bonuses and production boosts) for your next business venture (the next run). The more investment you put into your current civilization (getting more than 70 kittens), the larger the bonus you get for the next startup. In the end-game, you learn to manipulate time itself to fast-forward through years and maximize these compounded benefits.
